artifact_types.name: Reported Figure
artifact_types.description: One row per point-in-time number a source document actually states for a named metric: a quarterly series point, a weekly tracker point, or an FY-goal actual/target pair. This is the literal answer to 'what was X in period Y' - always prefer a matching row here over recomputing a figure from raw tables, or over citing a methodology document instead of the number itself.
coverage: every point-in-time figure stated for a named metric - quarterly, weekly, or snapshot alike
FY goal targets and their tracked actual/pace/status as their own rows
figures from MBR decks, dashboards, calendar exports, and verbatim summaries, not only formal marts
never compute or round a figure yourself - extract only values the source states

columns.name: metric_name
columns.description: Exact name of the reported metric (e.g. US conversion rate, Marketplace GMV, Care CSAT deflected).

columns.name: vertical_code
columns.description: Internal vertical code this figure belongs to, verbatim, or blank if company-wide.

columns.name: cut_dimension
columns.description: What the figure is broken out by, if anything: market, sub_vertical, fulfillment_type, benefit_count, theme, channel; blank for a top-line figure.

columns.name: cut_value
columns.description: The specific value of cut_dimension this row reports (e.g. US, Style, ship_to_home, 2+), or blank.

columns.name: fiscal_period
columns.description: The exact period this figure is as-of: a fiscal quarter label (e.g. Q2FY27) or a week-ending date, exactly as stated.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The reported numeric value itself, exactly as stated - never recomputed or rounded further.

columns.name: unit
columns.description: Unit of value: pct, usd, usd_millions, count, days, score, or as stated.

columns.name: yoy_or_qoq_pct
columns.description: Year-over-year or quarter-over-quarter change percent, if the source states one alongside the figure.

columns.name: target_value
columns.description: The FY goal/target for this metric, only if this row is a goal-tracking figure; blank otherwise.

columns.name: pct_of_goal
columns.description: Percent of target achieved, only if this row tracks a goal; blank otherwise.

columns.name: status
columns.description: AHEAD, BEHIND, BEAT, or ON_TRACK, only if this row tracks a goal and the source states a status; blank otherwise.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: The date this figure was reported or is accurate as-of, ISO format, if stated.

columns.name: source_note
columns.description: Where this number came from: document type or system (MBR deck, marketing calendar, Compass dashboard, etc).

artifact_types.name: Experiment Register
artifact_types.description: One row per experiment that ran an explicit control-vs-variant comparison: a true A/B test or holdout with a named control group, not merely a phased change. A staged or phased rollout with no control group is NOT an experiment - do not create a row for it. Extract from experiment trackers, Confluence PRDs, Jira tickets, Slack threads, and MBR notes alike. Never invent an experiment id or date the source does not state.
coverage: every experiment with an explicit control vs. variant/treatment comparison, even a brief status mention
exclude phased rollouts, staged launches, or ramps with no control group - those belong in Event Timeline
the exact experiment id if the source gives one, never invented
whether any other launch, campaign, or redesign overlapped the same window and vertical or market

columns.name: experiment_id
columns.description: The source's own experiment id in its exp_NNNN form (e.g. exp_2214), verbatim, never paraphrased. Never a Jira ticket, epic key, or other tracking-system id; if the source states no exp_NNNN id, leave blank rather than substitute one.

columns.name: experiment_name
columns.description: Exact experiment name/title as it appears in the source document.

columns.name: vertical_code
columns.description: The internal vertical code the experiment belongs to (e.g. US_CONV, SPEED, CARE), verbatim.

columns.name: hypothesis
columns.description: One-sentence hypothesis or goal of the test, as stated.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: Exact start date, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD, as stated in source.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Exact end date, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD, or blank if still running.

columns.name: status
columns.description: One of: running, shipped, killed, paused - exactly as the source states or clearly implies.

columns.name: primary_metric
columns.description: The metric the experiment was judged on, named exactly.

columns.name: owner
columns.description: Name of the person or team who owned or ran the experiment.

columns.name: confound_or_clean
columns.description: Whether another launch/campaign/change overlapped this experiment's window and vertical/market; name it, or state 'no concurrent launch found - clean read' if the source says so explicitly.

columns.name: decision_notes
columns.description: What was actually decided and on which number: shipped to what percent, on which readout figure, any caveat attached to the decision, as stated.

artifact_types.name: Experiment Readout
artifact_types.description: One row per metric reading actually OBSERVED for an experiment, on that experiment's own primary_metric only - never a different experiment's or an unrelated topic's figure. A confounded/deconfounded pair or a holdback reading is multiple rows, not one. Never store a forward-looking target, goal, or projection here - those belong in Reported Figure's target_value/pct_of_goal columns. Only extract what a source document actually states; never compute or estimate a reading.
coverage: every distinct OBSERVED reading for an experiment's own primary_metric, not only the headline one
a confounded/full-window reading AND a pre-confound or deconfounded reading when the source gives both
a holdback or control-only measurement as its own row
never a target, goal, or projected figure - those belong in Reported Figure, not here
never a reading that actually belongs to a different experiment or an unrelated topic in the same document

columns.name: experiment_id
columns.description: Matches the experiment_id in Experiment Register, verbatim. Never attribute a reading to this id when the source's surrounding context is a different experiment or an unrelated narrative.

columns.name: variant
columns.description: Treatment/control/holdback arm name, exactly as stated.

columns.name: metric_name
columns.description: Name of the metric this reading reports; must match this experiment_id's primary_metric in Experiment Register (e.g. conversion_lift, on_time_rate, benefit_awareness_30d) - omit the row if the source's reading is for a different metric.

columns.name: metric_value
columns.description: The numeric value of the reading, as stated (percent or point figure as given; do not convert units).

columns.name: unit
columns.description: Unit of metric_value: pct, pp, usd, score, or as stated.

columns.name: window_label
columns.description: Exactly one of: full_window, pre_confound, deconfounded, holdback - pick the closest fit. Never a target/goal/projected label (e.g. target_Q4FY26); targets are not readouts.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: Date the reading was taken or reported, ISO format.

columns.name: sample_size_units
columns.description: Number of units (sessions/orders/members) the reading is based on, if stated.

columns.name: is_significant
columns.description: 1 if the source states statistical significance, 0 if not significant or not stated.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Any caveat attached to this specific reading, e.g. what confounds it or what it isolates.

artifact_types.name: Event Timeline
artifact_types.description: One row per dated event that changed something a PM would care about: a launch, campaign, promo, budget change, org change, incident, restatement, or migration milestone. Extract from marketing-calendar exports, org announcements, Slack, postmortems, and meeting notes alike. The exact date is the point of this table - never estimate one.
coverage: every dated event, launch, campaign, incident, org change, or migration milestone stated
events mentioned only in passing - a calendar export line, a Slack aside
the exact date as stated; never estimate one

columns.name: event_name
columns.description: Short exact name of the event/launch/change, as stated in source.

columns.name: event_date
columns.description: Start or single date of the event, ISO format YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: End date if the event spans a range (a campaign, a phased rollout); blank for a single-day event.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: One of: campaign, launch, promo, holiday, budget_change, experiment_start, experiment_end, incident, org_change, restatement, migration, or the closest fit.

columns.name: vertical_code
columns.description: Internal vertical code affected, if any, verbatim (e.g. SPEED, CARE).

columns.name: market
columns.description: Market affected: US, CA, MX, or blank if company-wide/not market-specific.

columns.name: owner
columns.description: Person or team named as owner/driver of the event.

columns.name: planned_spend_usd
columns.description: Planned spend in USD if the event is a campaign/budget item and a figure is stated.

columns.name: actual_spend_usd
columns.description: Actual spend in USD if stated.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: One line on why this event matters or what it caused/coincided with, as stated.

artifact_types.name: Metric Definition Register
artifact_types.description: One row per named business metric or KPI. formula, canonical_value, and common_mistake are each VERBATIM-OR-BLANK: quote the source's exact words, or leave the cell BLANK if the source never states one - blank is correct, not a gap to fill. NEVER reconstruct, infer, or hedge ("not explicitly stated, but...", "presumably", "computed as") a value the text doesn't give. A row with a blank formula is still valid when other columns hold real stated content. Pair with Reported Figure for the actual number.
coverage: every named business metric or KPI the source defines or explains the calculation of
the precedence rule when two definitions or two systems disagree, if stated
formula, canonical_value, and common_mistake are each verbatim-or-blank - quote exact wording, never infer
a metric with a stated baseline/target but no stated method: blank formula, real canonical_value only
never a hedged formula ("not explicitly stated, but...", "presumably", "computed as") - blank beats a guess

columns.name: metric_name
columns.description: Canonical metric name, exactly as commonly referenced (e.g. blended on-time-to-promise, conversion rate, member CLTV).

columns.name: formula
columns.description: The exact calculation, as stated: the formula, ratio, or join logic in plain terms.

columns.name: source_tables
columns.description: The table(s) or mart(s) the metric is computed from, comma-separated, exact names.

columns.name: grain
columns.description: The row grain the metric is computed at (e.g. date x market x vertical x device).

columns.name: canonical_value
columns.description: The current correct reported value if the source states one, with its period.

columns.name: common_mistake
columns.description: The wrong way to compute or read this metric that the source warns against, stated concretely, with the wrong number if given.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Any other caveat: which definition wins when sources disagree, related metrics, or a precedence rule.

artifact_types.name: Warehouse Table Register
artifact_types.description: One row per base, dimension, or mart table documented in a schema doc or data dictionary: what it holds, and critically, whether its rows ARE the full real-world population or only a representative sample/panel of a larger true total. Get this wrong and every count on the table is wrong.
coverage: every base, dimension, and mart table named in a schema doc or data dictionary
whether it is a full population or a representative sample/panel, and of what true total

columns.name: table_name
columns.description: Exact table name as it appears in source (e.g. dim_member, fact_orders, member_cltv).

columns.name: table_category
columns.description: One of: dimension, base_fact, derived_mart.

columns.name: grain
columns.description: What one row of this table represents, stated plainly.

columns.name: row_count_in_table
columns.description: The row count or scale of the table ITSELF as stated (e.g. '120,000', '~730', '~2,500'), not the true population.

columns.name: population_type
columns.description: Exactly one of: full_population, representative_panel - whether this table's rows ARE the complete real-world set or a sample of a larger true population.

columns.name: true_population_estimate
columns.description: If population_type is representative_panel, the true real-world total this table samples from, as stated (e.g. '~14.2-14.6M active members'); blank if full_population.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Any warning about misusing this table, e.g. never COUNT(*) or SUM() it for a company-level total; where the true total comes from instead.

artifact_types.name: Roadmap Item
artifact_types.description: One row per roadmap card or ticket, from EITHER the legacy or the current tracking system - a query that only covers one system silently returns a partial roadmap. Extract from Aitable cards, Jira tickets, and Confluence PRDs alike.
coverage: every item from BOTH the legacy and the current ticketing system, never only one
the opened_date exactly as stated - it determines which system the item belongs in
cross-reference against any PRD naming the same item, if present

columns.name: item_title
columns.description: Exact title of the roadmap card/ticket, as stated.

columns.name: system
columns.description: Which tracking system holds this item: aitable or jira, exactly as the source names it.

columns.name: vertical_code
columns.description: Internal vertical code this item belongs to, verbatim.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Current status as stated (e.g. planned, in_progress, shipped, blocked).

columns.name: opened_date
columns.description: Date the item was opened/created, ISO format, if stated.

columns.name: owner
columns.description: Person or team named as owner of this roadmap item.

columns.name: one_line_description
columns.description: One-sentence description of what the item is/does.

artifact_types.name: Signal
artifact_types.description: A documented correction, precedence rule, or buried truth that changes how a headline metric, experiment readout, roadmap claim, or reported figure should be read. Name the metric/claim/table affected, the naive/headline reading, the corrected reading with exact figures and dates as stated, and the mechanism. Consolidate every mention of the same correction across all documents into one record; never invent a correction the source does not state.
coverage: the metric, table, experiment, or claim this correction affects, named exactly
the naive or headline reading, stated verbatim if the source gives one
the corrected reading, with exact figures and dates as stated
the mechanism: confound, definition change, mix-shift, join or sampling error, escalation lag, or precedence rule
which source or system wins when two systems disagree, if the source states a rule
any stale, draft, or superseded claim this corrects - state it must not be reported as current
